steps.description: Filter low-abundance genes first: compute each gene's mean log2 expression across all 12 samples and drop genes below a floor set at the low end of the distribution (state the floor and how it was chosen), or genes above the floor in fewer samples than the smallest group size (6). The filter must be computed without reference to the condition labels so it stays independent of the test. Do not re-normalize — the values already carry the core facility's normalization. Build the design matrix ~condition with the condition factor's reference level set explicitly to control by an explicit relevel call (never relying on alphabetical order), so a positive logFC means higher in treated. Fit lmFit, then eBayes with trend=TRUE and robust=TRUE. Extract the full results with topTable(coef for treated-vs-control, number=Inf, adjust.method='BH') and write a table of every tested gene with logFC, average expression, moderated t, raw p, BH-adjusted p. Report the number of genes tested after filtering and the number with adjusted p < 0.05. As a secondary, separately-labelled result, refit with treat(fit, lfc=1) and report the genes passing FDR 0.05 against that fold-change threshold — this is the effect-size question tested inside the model, not a post-hoc filter on the point estimates. Produce a volcano plot and a heatmap of the top significant genes (row-centred log2 values) and an MA-style plot of logFC vs average expression.

plan.title: Treated vs control muscle DE on log2 TPM (limma-trend)
plan.analytical_narrative: The input is a 12000 x 12 matrix of log2(TPM+1) values delivered by the core facility (/eval-eight-arms-with-log-normalized-n6-1/data/inputs/expression/log_expr.csv) with a 12-row sample table (metadata.csv) giving one condition column: 6 treated vs 6 control human muscle samples, unpaired, single batch. Because the values are already normalized log2 abundances and no counts exist, the negative-binomial route (DESeq2, edgeR, voom) is inapplicable — those models require raw integer counts, and back-transforming log2 TPM into pseudo-counts would fabricate a count structure the data does not have. The plan therefore runs limma with trend=TRUE and robust=TRUE on the delivered values, which is the method of record for log-scale expression. Step T1S1 establishes sample structure on the log values as delivered (PCA/MDS on the 500 most variable genes, sample-distance heatmap, per-sample detected-gene counts and value-range check) so any outlier or unexpected grouping is named before the model is fitted; it also verifies the values really are log2-scale (roughly 0-20, fractional) rather than a mislabelled count table. Step T1S2 filters low-abundance genes on mean log expression independently of the group labels, fits ~condition with control set explicitly as the reference level (so positive logFC = higher in treated), moderates with eBayes(trend=TRUE, robust=TRUE), and reports BH-adjusted p-values from topTable over all tested genes; an lfc-thresholded TREAT fit at log2FC 1 is run alongside as a secondary, FDR-controlled effect-size question rather than a post-hoc filter on the estimate. Step T1S3 writes the reproducibility record and the results tables. No enrichment step is planned: the research question asks only which genes differ, and pathway analysis would be unasked scope. With n=6 per group the design is modest but adequately replicated; power to detect small effects is limited and that should be stated in the report rather than compensated for with a relaxed threshold.
